[spoiler=secret meeting]The freezing of Oceanican assets by the United Lavian Republic came as a shock to Oceanicas political and business leaders. Even after the Lavian government lifted the freeze, the damage had been done. For many leaders in Oceanica, the event had proved that handling foreign governments could pose a threat to Oceanicas economy at any given time.

The Enclave Secret Government started secretly working on a long-term solution. In a secure underground chamber beneath the Enclave Pentagon, some of Oceanicas most influential leaders gathered for a classified briefing. The chamber was dark, with only a digital world map on the central table providing illumination. A senior Enclave director started speaking.

The Lavian incident has taught us something valuable. Oceanicas power is respected but not feared enough.
The room was silent as representatives from major research firms, defense contractors, and intelligence agencies listened intently.
We cannot have our economy, our technology, or our power be vulnerable again.

A second official leaned forward slightly.

Then we must ensure that no foreign government ever has the power to threaten Oceanica again. We have all come to agreement on The Enclave Great Plan. 

The Director nodded in agreement.

Following the tensions between the ULR and the USO, the Enclave continued to gain more power in the government of Oceanica and in the larger corporations of the country. Many of the larger corporations, worried that their assets in other countries might be seized or frozen, began to work closer with the leaders of the Enclave to secure the economy of Oceanica. Many of the larger technology and industrial companies, especially in the defense, aerospace, and research industries, continued to support the policies of the Enclave. This cooperation, although the existence of the Enclave was not officially acknowledged, allowed it to control the policies of the country behind the scenes.

The first phase of the Great Plan was to secretly change the global economy of Oceanica. In retaliation for the freezing of assets by the Lavians, the Enclave started to slowly cut ties with the ULR. Many of the investments and assets of the ULR, which were in Lavian territory, were slowly divested in complex corporate maneuvers. Many of the industrial ties with Lavian companies were slowly phased out, while capital and research ties were moved to other, more friendly, or more neutral countries. In reality, this was all part of the plan by the Enclave to secure the economy of Oceanica.

As these changes in economics were taking place, the Enclave was also pursuing technology leadership. The leaders of the Enclave knew that in order to have real influence in the world, they had to have science and tech leadership. There were backdoor funding systems that poured vast sums of money into advanced tech research facilities and companies that specialized in artificial intelligence, quantum computing, experimental physics, strategic energy technologies, and advanced defense technologies. These technologies were designed to ensure that Oceanica was always far ahead of the rest of the world in terms of technology.

However, the Enclave was working behind the scenes to extend Oceanican influence abroad. Rather than fighting other countries, Oceanican corporations and tech hubs invested even more heavily in their economic and tech networks with other countries. This brought many countries under the influence of Oceanican technology and finances. If any of these countries attempted to damage Oceanicas economy in the future, they would soon learn the price.

Within Oceanica itself, a subtle but definite shift began. While the public government maintained its neutrality in the face of growing international tensions, the Enclave advocated a stronger national position. Military projects expanded, collaboration between government agencies and private research firms increased, and key sectors received more funding and support. The aim was deterrence, not direct engagement. Oceanica would maintain its public position of stability and neutrality in the face of international tensions while building the tech, economic, and strategic power that would make any attack highly unlikely to succeed.

Secrecy remained the first and foremost principle of the Enclaves operations. Public declarations from the government continued to emphasize diplomacy, stability, and peaceful cooperation. The public face of Oceanica presented a neutral power that handled international tensions with care and prudence. At the same time, in hidden research facilities, corporate boardrooms, and secret intelligence agencies, the Enclaves Great Plan was quietly transforming the nations international influence.

As the meeting concluded in the underground facility, the Enclave Director stood beside the glowing world map.

The world will think Oceanica maintained its neutrality during the Lavian crisis.

He paused and turned to the officials assembled before him.

But tonight, we will make this nation great.[/spoiler]

[i][b]Official Public Statement from  Government of the United States of Oceanica[/b]
The Government of the United States of Oceanica recognizes that the United Lavian Republic has ended its temporary freezing of Oceanican assets within its jurisdiction. Oceanica regards this as an important move toward economic stability and the establishment of regular financial relations between our two countries.

While the situation lasted, Oceanica has taken a neutral stand regarding the overall conflict between the Elseyran Defense Union and the Commonwealth of Vespurias. Oceanica was not a party to the deliberations and determinations made by EDU member states regarding economic sanctions, and it still advocates for diplomatic dialogue and a peaceful resolution among all parties.

In the aftermath of the conflict, some Oceanican firms and banks have started reviewing their global investment strategies to ensure the protection of assets and trade flows in an increasingly challenging global environment. The Oceanican government endorses prudent economic planning while continuing to uphold its commitment to free trade, global cooperation, and respect for national sovereignty.

The United States of Oceanica is continuing to monitor the situation and remains committed to neutrality and constructive engagement with the global community.
[/i]

[Spoiler=[u][b]The Golden War, 1851-1853[/b][/u]]
The Golden War would become Lavia's first major geopolitical fiasco, almost severing the kingdom's closest ally, losing an important mining colony, and forever ruining King Fredrick's reputation. The incident had been brewing since the 1820's as more immigrants moved to New Aberdeen and Regalia, resulting in illegal border settlements inside Kantona as the large and relatively unimportant border to the Lavian crown lacked any proper enforcement. The issue worsened  after the 1846 discovery of gold in South Aberdeen, only encouraging further illegal migration into the border region although most of the immigrants were under the impression they were still within the borders of the Llyndorran Empire. 

Being made aware of the issue in 1848, King Fredrick began a campaign to begin taxing these illegal settlements in the attempt to make them somewhat legal, enforcing the taxation attempts with the threat of imprisonment, deportation, or reposition if they didn't pay. These tax collectors were not formally civil servants as a company of the Royal Kantona Guard was assigned to the task to protect the collectors from violence as well due to their knowledge of the local area. The only civil servant in this tax collection force was an official royal cartographer who would help identify if a border town was inside the borders of Kantona. Expectedly, these taxes were very unpopular within the border towns. During this attempt, Lavian and Llyndorran diplomats were locked in talks in an attempt to defuse the situation, however that fuse would be lit on New Years Day, 1851, when a battle between the garrison of a border town and the RKG company resulted in the town being almost completely burned and more than 40 militia members killed or wounded. 

The wider geopolitical community didn't expect either sides to actually take large actions and speculated the declaration was a symbolic action to bring Lavia to the negotiating table with less leverage, however King Fredrick didn't see it as such. It was his belief that, despite the royal family's close relation to Llyndorra's own royals, this was a ploy to cripple Lavia and make them dependent on Llyndorran imports. While the army was gathering and sailing to ports in Kanatona, the RKG would be ordered to viable border positions and would make the first real advances of the war once the main army was finally close by. The first real operation would begin in May of 1851 with the KRG launching a wide campaign to annex the mostly undefended border regions, only held by a few Llyndorran garrisons and militias. While the Lavian army was supposed to let the KRG do most of the work, the Llyndorran colonies had formed a contemporary army to defend against this wide advance, forcing the Lavian army's hand to participate in the battle which would later be known as Yulara Run, named after a creek where Lavian troops assaulted the Llyndorran camp. Yulara Run would result in a rousing early success for the Lavian army and KRG, with the calvary using heavy pistols to inflict heavy casualties on Llyndorran soldiers scrambling to get their weapons and defensive positions. The KRG would experience great success overall in this operation, annexing a significant amount of border territory as well as deporting illegal settlers who refused to pay taxes to these annexed towns, commonly only allowing them to take belongings needed for survival and taking the rest as payment for the unpaid taxes. While executions did happen during this time, they were few and far between and normally relegated only to those who fired upon Lavian civilians in retaliation for the invasion.

May of 1851 would see the Llynodrran army arrive and begin pushing back as the Lavian army mustered, leaving the KRG to handle most of the fighting against a more impressive foe. While the KRG would lose a significant amount of land they had taken, this was to allow for the Lavian army to make a spearhead advance and split the two Llyndorran colonies, cutting off a united chain of supply and increasing the time for supplies to reach New Aberdeen significantly. Fighting would remain roughly along these lines from August, 1851 to January, 1852 as Lavian forces nearly outstretched their supply lines to achieve the split and required further supply to be brought up before making the next move. Llyndorran forces would advance south as the Lavian army held the split, further battering the nearly exhausted KRG. Back in Lavia, King Fredrick's brother, Prince Rowan, was pressuring him to try to get Fredrick to the negotiating table. Rowan could see that if the war went badly for either side, it could lead to them loosing an extremely powerful ally, exactly the one they were now at war with. The public was already restless as many of them had relatives in Llyndorra and her colonies, some even in New Aberdeen and Regalia, and a longer war would only make the situation worse for the government, not to mention casualties.

King Fredrick would do the exact opposite however, ordering General Mardochée Picot to advance and capture Coores, the capitol of New Aberdeen. New Aberdeen would be pushed from both sides, losing significant amounts as well as needing to become a military mandate of Regalia after the capture of it's capitol on February 28th, 1852. The furthest extent of Lavia's gains would be seen by the success of this operation, however despite General Picot's attempts to reorganize his logistics chain to comply with the king's order, the Lavian army lacked a reliable supply chain and supplies were already heavily depleted by the offensive. The Llyndorran army however only built up more and more supply, dealing a serious blow to the the Lavian army at the Second Battle of Coores, forcing the retreat of General Picot in May of 1852. By September of the same year, both the KRG and the Lavian army had retreated so far south that Marigold City, the second main supply hub for the colony behind Southgate. Battered and bloodied by a bullet, General Picot would send his second in command, Lieutenant General Levi Redfield east with a sizeable force as well as much of the remaining KRG to retake the area north of Marigold City. Redfield would arrive in late September and lead a charge on Trentwell using his Joachim Halen Model 1846 Revolver, capturing the town as well as Puckaperra to the northeast in mid December. He and his forces would defend this territory till mid February, 1953, when the king ordered them to fall back and defend General Picot's retreating army as well as fortify Marigold city. 

During Redfield's defense, General Picot was caught in a pincer movement after naval raid on costal areas in the south turned into a full blow naval invasion by early December. He would retreat to Southgate by late December, and in mid January, 1853, the bloodiest battle of the war would occur. The Battle of Southgate marred both sides, nearly shattering the invasion force and dealing the final blow for Picot's army in the west. The colony's government evacuated to Marigold City alongside the army, heading to set up a war cabinet in Marigold City. While naval combat was always expected during the war, it surprisingly didn't break out. Llyndorra had practically the most powerful navy in the world at this point, but didn't want to risk the remaining goodwill between Lavia's navy, which was commanded by Prince Rowan. Each would have multiple faceoffs, but no shots were fired between navies throughout the war in large engagements, with small battles happening with no decisive victory over the other nation. Many historians think that if there had been large naval combat, Lavia might have been able to defend Kantona and hold out long enough for a white peace.

By this time, the war was wildly unpopular in Lavia, and King Fredrick had finally conceded to his brother Rowan. The kings of both nations met, along with their advisors, and for two months they debated and argued untill finally, on the 25th of April, 1853, King Fredrick and Queen Victoria signed the Kingsmount Armistice in the Commonwealth of Vespurias, handing over the Kantona colony officially to Llyndorra, in turn for reparations and Lavia retaining the mineral rights to the iron ore in what would later become the Hinterlands, Regerton, West Bank, Gilmore, (Metro) Southgate, Combes, Waverly, Hyrule, Kierley River, and Kantona districts of New Westmore. General Mackelby and his staff would meet General Picot and his staff as Lavian and KRG troops boarded ships to Lavia, with the generals exchanging swords as a show of respect and goodwill. This spawned a tradition which is still practiced between Llyndorran, Westmorian, and Lavian military ceremonies to this day. Lavian civilians would leave along with the army, however most of them being guaranteed their jobs with the agreement of mineral rights stayed in the region, creating a large lavian population in Suouther New Westmore to this day. Many KRG troops would stay as well due to having families or being born there, and as they were the default law in the wilder regions of Kantona, they would be pardoned by the Llyndorran and colonial governments, becoming sheriffs and rangers with their iconic Halen revolvers. King Fredrick, even with his reputation tarnished, would continue being the king of Lavia until he stepped down to put his daughter on the throne, a carefully planned move that was critical to clearing his legacy from failure.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=THE FOUNDING OF THE ERNHARDT SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE

RECOVERED]

[i]RELEASED JOINTLY BY THE ARELIAN DIRECTORATE FOR COMMUNICATION AND THE VALONIAN PRESS OFFICE.[/i]

THE ERNHARDT CHARTER

SECTION I - ESTABLISHES THE ERNHARDT SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE AS A SPECIAL ZONE AND INDEPENDENT ENTITY. CHARTING THE EXTENT OF THE ERNHARDT MOUNTAINS AS THE AREA OF THE ZONE, SIMILAR YET DIFFERENT TO THE FORMOSA SPECIAL ZONE OF THE FORMOSA BASIN.

THE ERNHARDT SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE (HEREAFTER THE ZONE) IS AIMED TO INVITE INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION IN NATIONAL EXTRACTION OPERATIONS AND SHARES SHALL BE SPLIT 2:1. IN THIS, NATURAL AUTHORITIES (THAT OF THE RESPONSIBLE, RIGHTFUL JURISDICTION) MAY BRING CORPORATE ENTITIES INTO LINE.

SECTION II - THE ZONE SHALL BE ADMINISTERED BY ADMINISTRATORS, ON BEHALF OF A BOARD OF MEMBER STATES, WHO SHALL VOTE ON DECISIONS OF THE ZONE.

SECTION III - FURTHER ZONE MEMBERS MAY BE ADMITTED,
WITH CANDIDACY AND FULL MEMBERSHIP RELYING ON MEETING CONDITIONS OF:

[list][*] DEMOCRACY, AND
[*] THE RULE OF LAW.[/list]

WHEN ALL CONDITIONS ARE FINALLY MET, A VOTE OF THE FULL BOARD SHALL FINALISE ITS DECISION. THE CANDIDATE MAY APPEAL TO THE BOARD, BUT MUST WAIT TO REAPPLY.

SECTION IV - ESTABLISHES THAT RENT SHALL BE SET AT AN EQUITABLE ~ FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF BUSINESS AND THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE ZONE, 
WITH THE RATES CHARGED EQUAL TO THE VALUE OF THE GOODS EXTRACTED AND THE RELIABLE SERVICES PROVIDED.
RENT MAY CHANGE THROUGH THE BOARD BUT RATES MUST GO THROUGH THE INTERNATIONAL FORUM.

SECTION V - POWER AND WATER SHALL BE PROVIDED BY AUTHORITIES, WITH PROVISIONS PROVIDED BY COMPANIES, STANDARDISED BY AUTHORITIES OF THE ZONE.

SECTION VI - ESTABLISHES THE ZONE SECURITY FORCE, CHARGED WITH THE SECURITY AND SAFETY OF THE ZONE AND ITS PERSONNEL. MEMBERS STATES SHALL MAKE CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE SECURITY FORCE AND A DISASTER FUND THROUGH SEPARATE CONTRIBUTIONS.

SECTION VII A - FOR SUMMARY CASES, PRE-TRIAL CRIMINALS SHALL BE RETURNED TO THEIR NATURAL JURISDICTION, WHERE THEY MAY FACE TRIAL.

SECTION VII B - FOR INDICTMENTS AND CIVIL DISPUTES ARISING FROM THE SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE, NATURAL JURISDICTIONS (NATIONAL) SHALL BE TURNED TO THE INTERNATIONAL COURT OF JUSTICE.

SECTION VIII - THE ONLY AUTHORISED EXTRACTION METHOD SHALL BE OF THAT SOLUTION MINING. EXTRACTORS MUST CONSIDER THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS OF AND DURING EXTRACTION, WITH LIMITS IMPOSED BY THE NATURAL JURISDICTION AND THE BOARD.

SECTION IX -  ESTABLISHES THAT IT IS THE DUTY OF THE EXTRACTOR TO REHABILIATE AND RECOVER THE ENVIRONMENT AND AREA. 
NO MATTER THE COST.

SECTION X - WITH ITS SIGNING, ITS SIGNATORIES SHALL BRING THE CHARTER INTO FORCE AND ALL PARTIES SHALL BE BROUGHT INTO LINE WITH IT. 

SIGNED

William Manor
[i]President of the Arelian Union[/i]
